base: data/consult-workups.json on content-r17-2026-11-11 after commit closing V3 (verify[] = [V4 only])

decisionRules.append.recommendation: Avoid antiplatelet, anticoagulant and other antithrombotic therapy, to prevent hemorrhagic stroke
evidenceNote: DADA2 consensus 2023 Delphi, statement 5.5: LOE 5 (D), agreement 8.3 of 9 (Lee 2023 Table 5)
Secondary hemorrhagic conversion of stroke has been documented (Lee 2023 p.7)

workup.append.test: DADA2: plasma or serum ADA2 enzyme activity; ADA2 sequencing
indication: Cryptogenic ischemic stroke, unexplained brain hemorrhage (including aneurysm) or spinal cord stroke in childhood or early adulthood (Lee 2023 Table 3, statement 3.5)
notes: Near-absent ADA2 activity is diagnostic; normal activity excludes DADA2 (Lee 2023 Table 2, statement 2.3)
Biallelic pathogenic or likely pathogenic ADA2 variants are diagnostic; one variant means a carrier (Lee 2023 Table 2, statements 2.4–2.5)
Standard sequencing can miss intronic, regulatory and copy-number variants; if suspicion remains, send enzyme activity or further genetic tests (Lee 2023 Table 2, statement 2.7)
ADA2 activity is measured by few laboratories; ADA2 is on most inborn-errors-of-immunity and autoinflammatory panels (Lee 2023 p.4)

sources.append: Lee PY, et al. Evaluation and Management of Deficiency of Adenosine Deaminase 2: An International Consensus Statement. JAMA Netw Open 2023;6(5):e2315894. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.15894
verify.remove: DADA2: ADA2 enzyme testing and treatment are not covered by the sources read

differential[12].clues.append: Treatable: TNF inhibitors lower the risk of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke (Lee 2023 p.6)

decisionRules.append.recommendation: Treat inflammation with glucocorticoids and/or a TNF inhibitor; consider a TNF inhibitor to prevent further strokes
evidenceNote: DADA2 consensus 2023 Delphi, statement 5.4: LOE 5 (D), agreement 7.7 of 9 (Lee 2023 Table 5)
Only TNF inhibitors have been shown to prevent further strokes (Lee 2023 p.7)
